title: Functions as values
description:
Write helpers that take and return functions, in `Funcs.java`:

```java
class Funcs {
    static <T> UnaryOperator<T> pipeline(List<UnaryOperator<T>> steps)       // applies the steps left to right
    static <T> Predicate<T> allOf(List<Predicate<T>> tests)                   // true when every test passes (true for none)
    static <T, R> Function<T, R> memoize(Function<T, R> f)                    // calls f once per distinct argument
    static Supplier<Integer> counter(int start, int step)                     // each get() returns the next value: start, start+step, ...
    static <T> Map<Boolean, List<T>> split(List<T> items, Predicate<T> test)  // {true=[matching], false=[others]}, order kept
}
```

Each call to `counter` or `memoize` returns an independent function with its own state.
hints: A lambda can only capture effectively final variables, but the object they refer to can change: `int[] next = {start};` lets the counter keep its state in `next[0]`.
`memoize` must check `containsKey` rather than `get(x) != null`, or a function that returns `null` would be called again every time.
